scope: Windows 11 x64 portable launch and native regression qualification; not product release acceptance

artifact.runtime_parity_with_acceptance: All previous bundle files are identical; only .node-version was added; launcher uses unchanged C# source with updated embedded manifest.

checks: embedded manifest and bundled runtime verified
changed, missing, additional files, manifest and junction rejected
bundled native read broker reads scoped fixture and rejects traversal without developer runtimes
fresh Windows DPAPI storage reaches subscription consent without developer tools or inherited Node options
same and relocated bundles reopen one host and preserve protected storage key
restart from relocated bundle preserves protected key and reacquires ownership

validation.native_broker_build: Rust 1.98.1, MSVC14.51, CRT static; PE dependencies kernel32, ntdll, api-ms-win-core-synch only
validation.native_launcher_build: Framework64 csc with warnings as errors; bundled Node24.21.0
validation.screenshot: native Windows Chrome setup consent screen inspected at 1280x900; no account connected
validation.trailing_output_separator: Full native build with an output path ending in a backslash passed; ZIP is outside the payload, every entry name and byte matches, and runtime manifest equals the recorded artifact.

retained_failures_and_resolution: Initial native build copy lacked contract schemas; copied required source assets and rebuilt successfully.

Initial native test copy lacked shared fixtures, then the pinned .node-version; added required source assets and reran the affected complete native suites. The package also now contains .node-version.
Initial package guard used an old markdown-it browser asset path; corrected against the installed package and actual HTTP asset route.
Initial external ZIP attempt could not represent upstream Unix-epoch timestamps; the build script now creates ZIP entries with a valid fixed timestamp.

Independent review reproduced a trailing-output-separator ZIP path bug; normalize the output path and reject drive/share roots, then rerun a complete native build and archive comparison with a trailing separator.
limitations: Native checks ran on the current Windows host with an isolated PATH, not a newly installed independent Windows machine.
First-run checks stop at subscription consent; no new account or real inference was invoked.
No installer signing, login startup, update/restore, physical phone delivery or public Google OAuth qualification is claimed.
The WSL production journal and account profiles were not migrated or changed.
